text: Based on the tool output, the 2021 tree-cover loss observed was 81.3 hectares, primarily in planted forests (68.1 hectares of Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda). The loss was not in native forests (0 hectares). According to Uruguay's forest laws, the felling of native forests requires authorization, but planted forests can be managed more flexibly. Since the loss occurred mainly in planted forests, it is likely that the activity was legal. However, further investigation would be needed to confirm if the remaining loss (13.2 hectares) occurred outside mapped forests and to verify if any permits were required for the planted forest management.
